title: Launch Orbit Scheduler — cross-product launch visibility grid and OKR alignment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Build a lightweight scheduler and shared visibility grid ("Launch Orbit") that maps all upcoming launch activities—runtime, console, API—onto a unified calendar correlated with OKRs and initiative milestones. The goal is to reduce cross-team friction, provide a single source of truth for capacity bookings, and surface OKR alignment (which launches impact which objectives).

Scope:
- Design a canonical grid view with lanes for Product, Engineering, Design, and Platform capacity; show per-launch estimated GPU/infra reservation, canary windows, and rollback windows.
- Integrate with existing Release Train calendar (read-only sync) and expose a small write API for capacity reservation requests.
- Add OKR tagging to launches (objective key + initiative name) and a filter to show OKR coverage and gaps.
- Ship a light-weight Slack notifier for owners when overlapping capacity requests are detected.

Outcomes & acceptance criteria:
- PMs and Eng leads can see overlapping capacity conflicts in a single screen with automated conflict flags.
- OKR-linked launches are surfaced in the grid; product leads can run a query to show which objectives are impacted by upcoming releases.
- Capacity reservation flow is implemented with a simple request/approval model; at least two teams (runtime and console) test the flow end-to-end in staging.
- Integration tests for calendar sync and conflict detection run in CI.

Deliverables:
- Launch Orbit UI (grid) v0.1 behind feature flag in Console.
- Small REST endpoint for reservation requests (spec + Swagger doc).
- Slack notifier configured with channel and escalation policy.
- Runbook for scheduling conflicts and owner contacts.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Kapoor (owner)
- Eng leads: Liam Chen (assignee), Priya Nair (runtime), Marco Silva (console)
- Design: Noor Patel
- Release ops: Hannah Ortiz

Success metrics (30/60/90):
- 30 days: UI shows >80% of scheduled launches for current quarter; two teams used reservation flow.
- 60 days: Conflict detection catches at least one real overlap and prevented a capacity contention incident.
- 90 days: Stakeholder satisfaction survey > 75% and reduction of cross-team scheduling emails by 50%.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Teams treat the grid as advisory only. Mitigation: Tie capacity reservation to Dedicated capacity booking workflow and require acknowledgement in release checklist.
- Risk: Calendar sync duplication with existing release-train docs. Mitigation: read-only sync and de-duplicate by matching on release IDs.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1–2: Prototype grid with mocked reservations; gather PM/Eng feedback.
- Week 3–4: Implement API + staging integration with runtime and console teams.
- Week 5: Canaries with a small cohort of launches; monitor conflict detection.
- Week 6: Full opt-in for Q2 launch planning and retro for improvements.

Follow-ups:
- Extend to automated capacity hedging recommendations (Optimize integration).
- Add RBAC and audit trail for on-prem/private customers if adopted.
